---
title: "Solutions: Extra practice: linear regression"
---

::: {.callout-note}
These are the solutions to the
[Extra practice: linear regression](../lecture-02/08-practice-linear-regression.qmd) exercises.
Try each exercise yourself before you look.
:::

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(medicaldata)
```

We make `opt_clean` and `bw_fit` the same way as the exercise page.

```{r}
opt_clean <- opt |>
  mutate(
    Birth.outcome = str_trim(Birth.outcome),
    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("C", "T"),
                   labels = c("control", "treatment"))
  ) |>
  filter(Birth.outcome == "Live birth") |>
  select(PID, Clinic, Group, Age, BMI, Birthweight, GA.at.outcome)

bw_fit <- linear_reg() |>
  fit(Birthweight ~ Group, data = opt_clean)

bw_tidy <- tidy(bw_fit, conf.int = TRUE)
bw_tidy
```

## Exercise 1: The same as a t-test

```{r}
t.test(Birthweight ~ Group, data = opt_clean, var.equal = TRUE)
```

The t statistic has the same size as the regression's
(the sign flips because `t.test()` subtracts treatment from control),
and the p-value is identical.
A regression with one two-level predictor
is a two-sample t-test with equal variances.

## Exercise 2: Add covariates

```{r}
bw_fit_adj <- linear_reg() |>
  fit(Birthweight ~ Group + Age + BMI + Clinic, data = opt_clean)

bw_adj_tidy <- tidy(bw_fit_adj, conf.int = TRUE)
bw_adj_tidy
glance(bw_fit_adj)
```

**(2)** The model used `r glance(bw_fit_adj)$nobs` of `r nrow(opt_clean)` rows,
because the model drops the `r sum(is.na(opt_clean$BMI))` rows with missing BMI.

**(3)** The treatment estimate moves from `r round(bw_tidy$estimate[2])`
to `r round(bw_adj_tidy$estimate[2])` g,
and its confidence interval still includes 0.
Randomization balances the covariates between groups,
so adjusting for them barely changes the treatment effect.

## Exercise 3: Check the fit

```{r}
augment(bw_fit, new_data = opt_clean) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .pred, y = .resid)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 5, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  labs(x = "Fitted birth weight (g)", y = "Residual (g)")
```

With one two-level predictor there are only two fitted values.
The residuals are skewed,
with a long tail of babies born much lighter than average,
often preterm.

## Exercise 4: Gestational age

```{r}
ga_fit <- linear_reg() |>
  fit(GA.at.outcome ~ Group, data = opt_clean)
ga_tidy <- tidy(ga_fit, conf.int = TRUE)
ga_tidy

ga_fit_adj <- linear_reg() |>
  fit(GA.at.outcome ~ Group + Age + BMI + Clinic, data = opt_clean)
ga_adj_tidy <- tidy(ga_fit_adj, conf.int = TRUE)
ga_adj_tidy
```

Treatment changed gestational age by `r round(ga_tidy$estimate[2], 1)` days
(95% CI `r round(ga_tidy$conf.low[2], 1)` to `r round(ga_tidy$conf.high[2], 1)`),
and by `r round(ga_adj_tidy$estimate[2], 1)` days after adjusting.
There's no evidence of an effect,
which matches the trial's published result.
